lockfile | default: Checks: the dependency list package-lock.json for known vulnerabilities and malware, with Trivy and OSV, plus Grype if it is installed. It reads the file; nothing is installed or run.
Also checks: each vulnerability it finds for signs of exploitation (CISA KEV, FIRST EPSS and public exploit indexes), to suggest what to fix first.
Also checks: when each fix was published, to measure how long fixes have been available.

Flags: any language package version (npm, PyPI, Maven, Go and the others deps.dev covers) published in the last 7 days; OS packages are not checked. New releases are when compromised versions are live, before advisories catch up.
Fails: never on what it finds: it exits 0 when the run completes. For CI, add a pass or fail check.
Writes: findings.csv, summary.md, assessment.json and report.html to r.
Writes: The scanners' own output goes in r/raw.
Contacts: OSV: sends package names and versions, and advisory IDs.
Contacts: deps.dev: sends package names and versions.
Contacts: CISA KEV, if it finds vulnerabilities: sends nothing (it downloads the whole list).
Contacts: FIRST EPSS, if it finds vulnerabilities: sends CVE IDs.
Contacts: Exploit indexes on GitHub and GitLab, if it finds vulnerabilities: sends CVE IDs.

Contacts: Fix-date records (Debian, Ubuntu, Red Hat, Alpine, Packagist and Go), if it finds vulnerabilities: sends package names, fixed versions and advisory IDs, and your GITHUB_TOKEN to GitHub if it is set.
Contacts: Trivy and Grype download their vulnerability databases from their own servers, unless their copy is fresh.
Contacts: For a pom.xml, Trivy fetches the parent and dependency POMs from Maven Central and from any repository the pom.xml or your Maven settings name.
Contacts: Your files are read on your computer. Apart from what the scanners fetch, only the names and IDs listed are sent.
Doesn't check: the project's health: add where its source is on GitHub.
Doesn't check: the project's own code, or whether what you install (for example a .vsix from the VS Code Marketplace) was built from this source: only the listed dependencies are checked.
Doesn't check: that the scanners on your computer are the genuine releases: pin their versions and hashes under All options.
Doesn't check: whether the vulnerable code is reachable where you run it: a finding is a version match, not proof of exposure.

Also checks: each vulnerability it finds for signs of exploitation (CISA KEV, FIRST EPSS and public exploit indexes), to suggest what to fix first.
Also checks: when each fix was published, to measure how long fixes have been available.

Flags: any language package version (npm, PyPI, Maven, Go and the others deps.dev covers) published in the last 7 days; OS packages are not checked. New releases are when compromised versions are live, before advisories catch up.
Flags: a suggested likelihood from 1 to 5, built from the findings and the project's signals. It is a starting point for an assessor, not a risk rating.
Fails: never on what it finds: it exits 0 when the run completes. For CI, add a pass or fail check.
Writes: findings.csv, summary.md, assessment.json and report.html to r.
Writes: The scanners' own output goes in r/raw.
Contacts: OSV: sends package names and versions, and advisory IDs.
Contacts: deps.dev: sends package names and versions.
Contacts: Maven Central, PyPI or npm, for a JAR, wheel, sdist or npm .tgz: sends the file's package name and version.
Contacts: CISA KEV, if it finds vulnerabilities: sends nothing (it downloads the whole list).
Contacts: FIRST EPSS, if it finds vulnerabilities: sends CVE IDs.
Contacts: Exploit indexes on GitHub and GitLab, if it finds vulnerabilities: sends CVE IDs.

Contacts: Fix-date records (Debian, Ubuntu, Red Hat, Alpine, Packagist and Go), if it finds vulnerabilities: sends package names, fixed versions and advisory IDs, and your GITHUB_TOKEN to GitHub if it is set.
Contacts: Trivy and Grype download their vulnerability databases from their own servers, unless their copy is fresh.
Contacts: Your files are read on your computer. Apart from what the scanners fetch, only the names and IDs listed are sent.

Doesn't check: that the scanners on your computer are the genuine releases: pin their versions and hashes under All options.
Doesn't check: whether the vulnerable code is reachable where you run it: a finding is a version match, not proof of exposure.
